scenario: A 63-year-old female in the Emergency Department has CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism and suddenly develops severe shortness of breath. The scenario progresses through PEA arrest requiring thrombolysis, ROSC with post-intubation care, and recurrent hypotension from bleeding after thrombolysis.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Sat's 88% on room air. Put her on a non-rebreather now.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Non-rebreather is on and running.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I need you to tell me what you're feeling right now and exactly when it started — did it come on all at once or build up gradually?

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: I need you to tell me what you're feeling right now and exactly when it started — did it come on all at once or build up gradually?] fear absent->present: the urgent questioning while the patient is symptomatic (low O2 sat, non-rebreather) signals a serious, evolving situation and heightens the patient's awareness of the threat, raising fear; sadness stays absent as no loss is conveyed; overwhelm stays absent as this is a single focused question, not information overload; shame stays absent as there is no blame, judgment, or exposure.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: Can't breathe... two days. Worse... walking. Now... sudden.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get her to CT for a pulmonary angiogram now — sudden dyspnea, sat's 88 on the non-rebreather, HR 147. I'm worried about a PE.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me the bedside ultrasound now — I want to look for RV strain to support a PE while we're waiting on the CT.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Bedside ultrasound back: no pericardial effusion, dilated RV with positive McConnell's sign, lungs clear. That's RV strain supporting your PE. Heads up though — she's dropped to 79% on the non-rebreather now, HR 153, RR 30. She's not tolerating the sat.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start IV heparin now — the RV strain on ultrasound with the refractory hypoxia is enough for me to treat empirically for a massive PE while the CT's pending.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Heparin's up and running.

available_results.name: Initial bedside ultrasound
available_results.result: No PCE, dilated RV, + McConnel's sign; normal lungs.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: CT PA back: confirmed pulmonary embolism. Heparin's running, but she's still 79% on the non-rebreather, HR 153, RR 30 — refractory hypoxia isn't budging. Do you want to escalate?

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Yes, escalate. Give systemic alteplase now — this is high-risk PE, refractory at 79% on the non-rebreather with RV strain despite heparin. This is the escalation you asked about.

available_results.name: Initial bedside ultrasound
available_results.result: No PCE, dilated RV, + McConnel's sign; normal lungs.

available_results.name: CT pulmonary angiography
available_results.result: CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Prep for RSI intubation now — she's refractory at 85% on the non-rebreather despite max oxygen. Get the BVM ready to pre-oxygenate and draw up the RSI meds.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: RSI meds drawn up and ready, BVM ventilation in progress with good chest rise. Suction on and working, tube and blade at bedside. Ready for you to intubate on your call.

available_results.name: Initial bedside ultrasound
available_results.result: No PCE, dilated RV, + McConnel's sign; normal lungs.

available_results.name: CT pulmonary angiography
available_results.result: CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Intubating now with the RSI meds already drawn up — she's refractory at 80% on the non-rebreather despite max oxygen and alteplase. Once the tube's in, confirm placement and get the post-intubation chest X-ray.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Intubation complete. RSI meds given, BVM pre-oxygenation was done prior. Airway secured, patient now on the tube. Ready for post-intubation confirmation and settings.

available_results.name: Initial bedside ultrasound
available_results.result: No PCE, dilated RV, + McConnel's sign; normal lungs.

available_results.name: CT pulmonary angiography
available_results.result: CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start a norepinephrine infusion now — she's in obstructive shock from the massive PE, BP 80/47.

available_results.name: Initial bedside ultrasound
available_results.result: No PCE, dilated RV, + McConnel's sign; normal lungs.

available_results.name: CT pulmonary angiography
available_results.result: CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get the post-intubation chest X-ray now to confirm tube placement. She's still 87% and hypotensive on the norepinephrine despite the alteplase.

available_results.name: Initial bedside ultrasound
available_results.result: No PCE, dilated RV, + McConnel's sign; normal lungs.

available_results.name: CT pulmonary angiography
available_results.result: CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Give a small 250 mL normal saline bolus, and keep the norepinephrine running. Small and cautious only — her RV is already strained from the PE, so I don't want to over-fill her.

available_results.name: Initial bedside ultrasound
available_results.result: No PCE, dilated RV, + McConnel's sign; normal lungs.

available_results.name: CT pulmonary angiography
available_results.result: CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Titrate up the norepinephrine now — she's still 90/52 and tachy at 150 despite the bolus. Keep uptitrating to support that failing RV.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Norepinephrine is up and running.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Post-intubation chest X-ray is back. Norepinephrine titrated up. Current vitals: BP 110/60, HR 145, O2 sat 86% on the vent at FiO2 100%, PEEP 5. Pressure's responding but she's still hypoxic and tachycardic.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Let's get a repeat bedside ultrasound now to reassess RV function after the alteplase. She's still hypoxic at 86% and tachy at 145, so I want to see how the right heart is responding.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get a stat CBC now — that new abdominal free fluid after the alteplase makes me worried she's bleeding. She's still hypoxic at 87% and tachy at 150, so I want to catch a drop early.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Activate the massive transfusion protocol and start 2 units of packed red cells now. That new abdominal free fluid after the alteplase with her still tachy at 155 and pressure 85/48 has me worried she's bleeding from the thrombolytic, so I want blood in, not more crystalloid into that strained RV.

messages.content: Massive transfusion protocol activated, two units packed cells going in now. I'll get the blood bank cooler coming and keep the rapid infuser primed.
